problem.text: Three unit squares and two line segments connecting two pairs of vertices are shown. What is the area of $\triangle ABC$?

steps.title: Where to start: check the angle where the segments cross
steps.body: The figure lives on a grid of unit squares, so the slopes of the two segments are easy to read, and slopes tell you whether they cross at a right angle. Call $E$ the bottom-left corner of the lower-left square and $D$ its bottom-right corner, so $D$ is straight below $B$ and $BD = 2$. Put $E$ at $(0,0)$; then $A = (0,2)$, $B = (1,2)$, and segment $AC$ ends at the corner $(2,1)$.

your_turn.prompt: What are the slopes of line $BE$ and of line $AC$?
your_turn.answer: $BE$ goes from $(0,0)$ to $(1,2)$: slope $2$. $AC$ goes from $(0,2)$ to $(2,1)$: slope $-\tfrac{1}{2}$.

steps.title: A right triangle at $C$
steps.body: The slopes multiply to $2\cdot\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right) = -1$, so the segments are perpendicular and $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$. That makes $\triangle ABC$ a right triangle with hypotenuse $AB = 1$, so its area is half the product of the legs $BC$ and $AC$.

steps.title: Similar triangles give $BC$
steps.body:
$AB$ and $ED$ are both horizontal, so the transversal $BE$ makes $\angle ABC = \angle BED$ (alternate angles). Both triangles also have a right angle ($C$ and $D$), so $\triangle ACB \sim \triangle BDE$, with $A \leftrightarrow B$, $C \leftrightarrow D$, $B \leftrightarrow E$. Matching hypotenuse to hypotenuse and the side next to the equal angle:
$$\frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{ED}{BE}.$$

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
By the Pythagorean theorem in $\triangle ABC$, $AC^2 = 1 - \tfrac{1}{5} = \tfrac{4}{5}$, so $AC = \tfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$. The area is
$$\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\cdot\tfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}} = \tfrac{1}{5}.$$
The answer is **(B)**.
